commonsFile: File:Caminito del Rey, Málaga, España, 2023-05-18, DD 12.jpg
attribution: Diego Delso — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Caminito del Rey, El Chorro gorge, Málaga province
alt: The Caminito del Rey walkway clinging to the wall of the Gaitanes gorge
caption: The Caminito del Rey walkway hangs on the wall of the Gaitanes gorge above the Guadalhorce river. Day 2 opening walk, about three hours one way along a timed, ticketed route (children under 8 not admitted).

commonsFile: File:Panorámica Alhambra y Sierra Nevada de fondo.jpg
attribution: Er Komandante — CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The Alhambra fortress-palace on its hill with the snow-covered Sierra Nevada behind
caption: The Alhambra with the snow-capped Sierra Nevada behind it: the view that defines this route, where a palace city and a 3,000 m range sit within an hour's drive of each other. Days 5–6 in Granada, before the climb to the Alpujarras.

attribution: Jalovisko — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Puente Nuevo bridge spanning the El Tajo gorge at Ronda
caption: Ronda's Puente Nuevo spans the 100 m-deep El Tajo gorge that splits the old town in two. Day 2 evening and Day 3 morning, with gorge-floor paths below the bridge.

commonsFile: File:Setenil de las Bodegas Cadiz Spain.jpg
attribution: Jialiang Gao www.peace-on-earth.org — CC BY-SA 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Setenil de las Bodegas, Cádiz province
alt: Whitewashed houses built under overhanging rock at Setenil de las Bodegas
caption: At Setenil de las Bodegas houses and bars are built straight into the overhanging rock of the Trejo river gorge. A short stop on Day 3 on the drive from Ronda towards Córdoba.

attribution: Alvaro.vinuela.carnicero — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Red-and-white horseshoe arches inside the Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba
caption: The forest of striped double arches in Córdoba's Mezquita, begun in 784 and later enclosing a Renaissance cathedral. Day 4 is spent in Córdoba, including Medina Azahara outside the city.

attribution: Mark Chinnick — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Whitewashed flat-roofed houses of Capileira beneath the Sierra Nevada
caption: Capileira, the highest village of the Poqueira valley, with its flat-roofed Berber-style houses under the Sierra Nevada. Base for Days 7–8, with the irrigation-channel walk to Bubión and Pampaneira.

attribution: Tuxyso / Wikimedia Commons — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Panorama of Trevélez, a high mountain village in the Alpujarras
caption: Trevélez, among the highest villages in Spain, known for its air-cured mountain ham. Day 9 stop on the way east out of the Alpujarras.

commonsFile: File:Alcazaba, Punta de la Cornisa y Mulhacén 3.479 m.jpg
attribution: Juanjosepascua — CC BY-SA 3.0 es, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Snow-covered summits of Alcazaba and Mulhacén in the Sierra Nevada
caption: Alcazaba and Mulhacén (3,479 m), the highest summits of mainland Spain. In February–March they carry real snow, so the trip uses guided snowshoe walking at the lower levels rather than a summit attempt.

photographer: Luis Daniel Carbia Cabeza from Almeria, Spain
attribution: Luis Daniel Carbia Cabeza from Almeria, Spain — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Badlands of the Tabernas desert in Almería province
caption: The eroded badlands of the Tabernas desert, one of the driest places in Europe and a former spaghetti-western film set. Day 9–10 crossing between the Alpujarras and the coast.

commonsFile: File:Panorama of Playa de los Genoveses in Cabo de Gata.jpg
attribution: 3rik A. — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Playa de los Genoveses, Cabo de Gata-Níjar Natural Park
alt: Wide undeveloped sandy beach at Los Genoveses in Cabo de Gata
caption: Los Genoveses, an undeveloped dune-backed bay in the Cabo de Gata-Níjar Natural Park. Day 11 walking and campsite base at the end of the loop; swimming is not the point in March.

commonsFile: File:Overview of the Rodalquilar gold mine leaching tanks (2026).jpg
attribution: Paul Colin Hennig firstdorsal.eu — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Rodalquilar gold mine, Cabo de Gata-Níjar
alt: Concrete leaching tanks of the abandoned Rodalquilar gold mine
caption: The abandoned leaching tanks of the Rodalquilar gold mine in the volcanic hills of Cabo de Gata. Day 10 stop that shows the park's mining and volcanic history, not just its beaches.

attribution: Palickap — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The whitewashed Albaicín quarter of Granada seen from the Alhambra
caption: The Albaicín, Granada's medieval Moorish quarter, seen across the valley from the Alhambra. Day 5 evening walk through its lanes and viewpoints.
